content: 1. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug in this case. 2. Co-administration of ixazomib with strong CYP3A inhibitors did not result in clinically meaningful changes in systemic exposure to ixazomib during clinical trials. However, the interaction is considered minor, and its significance is unknown. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ketamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. 5. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. 12. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions to CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Clarithromycin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 16. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 17. Clarithromycin and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 19. Clarithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 24. Clarithromycin and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Lofepramine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and lofexidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it significantly increases lomitapide levels. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase lorlatinib to the previous dose after three plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Clarithromycin and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in increased lurasidone exposure and the potential for serious adverse reactions. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before co-administration. 39. Clarithromycin and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 milliseconds in the corrected QT interval. Allow sufficient washout time of drugs known to prolong the QT interval before administering macimorelin. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 41. Maprotiline and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. 48. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
